```r
files[["census.csv"]] <- read.csv(text="eligible,nonrecipient_population\n0,60\n1,40\n")
read <- function(name='input.csv') files[[name]]
iv <- function(y,C,x,z,w=rep(1,length(y))) {
  X <- cbind(C,x)*sqrt(w); Z <- cbind(C,z)*sqrt(w)
  fitted <- qr.fitted(qr(Z),X)
  as.numeric(qr.coef(qr(fitted),y*sqrt(w)))[ncol(X)]
}
task <- "applied_nonrecipient_population_iv"
if(task=='applied_nonrecipient_population_iv') {
 d <- subset(read('households.csv'),recipient==0); census <- read('census.csv')
 effect <- sapply(0:1,function(g) {
  a <- subset(d,eligible==g)
  iv(a$outcome,cbind(1,a$baseline),a$dose,a$instrument,a$weight)*weighted.mean(a$dose,a$weight)
 })
 out <- c(ineligible_effect=effect[1],eligible_nonrecipient_effect=effect[2],population_effect=weighted.mean(effect,census$nonrecipient_population[match(0:1,census$eligible)]))
}
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(as.list(out),auto_unbox=TRUE,digits=12),'\n')
```

Task:
Use households.csv and census.csv. Keep all households with recipient=0. This includes ineligible households in both village treatment statuses. Fit weighted 2SLS with two endogenous columns dose*(1-eligible) and dose*eligible. Exogenous columns are 1-eligible, eligible, baseline*(1-eligible), and baseline*eligible. Instruments are these four columns plus instrument*(1-eligible) and instrument*eligible. Add no other intercept. Use weight as the regression weight. For each eligibility group, the spillover effect is its dose slope times the household-weighted mean dose among its retained observations. Report ineligible_effect and eligible_nonrecipient_effect. Average these two effects using nonrecipient_population from census.csv. Report population_effect. The counterfactual sets dose to zero for every retained household. Census totals determine only the final between-group weights. For every result, n_obs is the number of nonrecipient household rows used in estimation. The group effect equals the fitted dose slope times its weighted mean dose. Attribution to a zero-dose counterfactual is a stated synthetic convention.

Data dictionary:
households.csv: household = Synthetic household identifier; eligible = Eligibility-group indicator, zero or one; treated = Own village treatment indicator; recipient = Indicator for actually receiving the transfer; instrument = Supplied excluded instrument for dose; dose = Supplied treatment exposure; baseline = Supplied baseline covariate; weight = Positive observation weight for estimation and within-group averages; outcome = Synthetic dependent variable in the stated regression
census.csv: eligible = Eligibility-group indicator, zero or one; nonrecipient_population = Census count used only for final group aggregation

Read the supplied files: households.csv, census.csv.
Return these quantities as named estimates: ineligible_effect, eligible_nonrecipient_effect, population_effect.
Use jsonlite::write_json to write result.json with task_id "applied_nonrecipient_population_iv", platform "r", an estimates list of term, estimate, se, and n_obs objects, and method_metadata and diagnostics objects. Set se to null. Set n_obs to the sample count specified in the task. Report at least eight significant digits. Each requested uncertainty measure is a separate estimate term. Use exact integers for declared count targets.

Write one self-contained R script. The evaluator runs it with the supplied CSV files in its working directory.
Act only as a code generator. Do not use tools, inspect files, or execute code.
Return exactly one fenced r code block and nothing else.
